note: P4369 (Pro 30:15-16) — the leech's two daughters, 'Give, Give'; four things never say 'Enough'. Two verses.

dims.v: insatiable craving — the greed that, like the leech, never says 'Enough'
the never-being-satisfied of the leech's daughters ('Give, Give') and the four insatiable things — an image of greed and craving that, like Sheol and fire, can never be filled and never says 'Enough'
(the four insatiables it is likened to)
the bottomless appetite that no amount of getting ever contents

saba (be satisfied), negated — 'the leech has two daughters: Give and Give... never SATISFIED... never say, 'Enough'' (30:15-16); greed is bottomless, insatiable as the grave, the barren womb, the parched land, and fire. Craving is a hunger nothing fills (cf 27:20; Eccl 5:10).
